title: Quotient-level inverse-image tensor unit and associator
statement: Let $O$ be any commutative ring and $t\in O$, and $g:V\to W$ any morphism of schemes. Let P_W and P_V be the normalized strict etale evaluation packages, A the ordinary inverse/direct image package for g, and E the derived image package [def-per-strict-etale-system-interfaces, def-pur-coefficient-system-image-data]. Write T^W_{r,m}, T^V_{r,m} for their selected derived quotient scalar extensions, I_n for the level-n inverse image, u^W_n,u^V_n for the selected multiplication unitors and a^W,a^V for the selected balanced associators. The normalized comparison d_{r,m}: I_m T^W_{r,m} ≅ T^V_{r,m} I_r satisfies, for every derived input P, d_{n,n}(P) followed by u^V_n(I_n P) = I_n(u^W_n(P)), and I_n(a^W_{r,m,n}(P)) followed by d_{r,n}(P) = d_{m,n}(T^W_{r,m}P) followed by T^V_{m,n}(d_{r,m}(P)) followed by a^V_{r,m,n}(I_r P). All indices may repeat; no boundedness, regularity, completeness, coefficient finiteness or quotient-map flatness is required.

source.place: Zheng Construction 4.1, printed p. 21, and Lemma 5.16, printed pp. 34--35; Stacks Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition. Agent extraction of the left-functor calculation underlying the Brown coefficient coherence proof.

proof.text: Work first on ordinary modules. The ordinary inverse-image lift and its restriction comparison are fixed on underlying sheaves, including all constant generators. Scalar transposition detects equality after the insertion x↦1 tensor x. The tensor_unit normalization therefore pins the inverse-image tensor comparison. The multiplication unitor takes scalar insertion to the identity, while the balanced associator takes two successive insertions to the direct one. Transpose the two comparison words: the underlying restriction comparisons compose as identities, so the transposes are equal. This proves the ordinary unit and composition squares, including identity maps.

Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution P. Exact geometric inverse image and coefficient extension preserve flat-term K-flat complexes. The selected derived comparisons satisfy derivedTensor_rep, derivedUnit_rep and derivedAssoc_rep. Postcompose the composition square with the inverse-image factorization and the scalar computation map for the direct quotient extension. Use naturality to move the successive scalar computation maps and apply the three representative equations. The resulting equality is Q of the ordinary square from step 1, degree by degree. All the postcomposed maps are invertible on these resolving complexes, so cancel them. The same calculation using the multiplication unitor proves the unit square.

Every derived object is isomorphic to Q of a flat-term K-flat resolution. Naturality of each entire comparison word transports both identities across the isomorphism. The existing coefficientPullbackCoherence theorem supplies the corresponding calculation for the all-ring-sheaf normalization model; the representative calculation above is the transport to the selected quotient-level packages, rather than any new choice of a scalar unit or associator.

lean.statement:
theorem strictEtaleInverseTensorCoherence
    {O : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing O] {t : O}
    {V W : Scheme.{u}} (g : V ⟶ W)
    (PW : StrictEtaleEvaluation W O t) (PV : StrictEtaleEvaluation V O t)
    (A : StrictEtaleOrdinaryImage O t g)
    (E : CoefficientSystemDerivedImage.{u + 1, u, u + 1, u, u + 1, u + 2}
      O t _ _ _ A PW PV) :
    (∀ (n : ℕ) P,
      (E.derivedTensor (Nat.le_refl n)).hom.app P ≫
        (PV.derivedUnit n).hom.app ((E.level n).inverse.obj P) =
      (E.level n).inverse.map ((PW.derivedUnit n).hom.app P)) ∧
    (∀ {r m n : ℕ} (h₁ : m ≤ r) (h₂ : n ≤ m) P,
      (E.level n).inverse.map ((PW.derivedAssoc h₁ h₂).hom.app P) ≫
        (E.derivedTensor (h₂.trans h₁)).hom.app P =
      (E.derivedTensor h₂).hom.app ((PW.scalar h₁).derived.obj P) ≫
        (PV.scalar h₂).derived.map ((E.derivedTensor h₁).hom.app P) ≫
        (PV.derivedAssoc h₁ h₂).hom.app ((E.level r).inverse.obj P))
